clue.text: Grub to provide food and support

parts.note: to cater is to supply food, as for a party
a pillar is an upright that holds a structure up

explanation.surface: A caterer's job description: feeding people and propping them up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grub' looks like slang for food, which suits the catering, but it is the definition: a larva.
explanation.definitionFit: A grub is an insect larva, and a butterfly's larva is the familiar example.

clue.text: All that is required for the honeymoon departure?

definitions.text: All that is required for the honeymoon departure?

parts.words: All that is required for the honeymoon departure
parts.note: a newly wed couple traditionally drove off in a horse-drawn coach

explanation.surface: A checklist for a newly married couple setting off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pair' does double duty: the two horses, and the couple.
explanation.definitionFit: A coach drawn by two horses was the classic grand transport for newlyweds leaving the wedding.

clue.text: Infant raised to do simple arithmetic

parts.note: a tot is a small child
raised means lifted up

explanation.surface: A small child brought up to manage basic sums.
explanation.definitionFit: Adding a column of figures to get a total is elementary arithmetic.

clue.text: Managed to hold the first man coming up fast

indicators.note: to hold says the first piece encloses the next

parts.note: to run something is to manage it

indicators.note: coming up in a down clue says the name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Adam was the first man in the Bible

explanation.surface: An organiser making room for an early fast arrival.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'coming up' reads the name from bottom to top. 'fast' looks like speed but is the definition: a period without food.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramadan is the Muslim month of fasting from dawn to sunset.

clue.text: Sort of investigation made by bathyscape?

definitions.text: Sort of investigation made by bathyscape?

parts.words: Sort of investigation made by bathyscape
parts.note: a bathyscape is a deep-sea diving vessel, so its exploration takes place far down

explanation.surface: Asking what kind of study a deep-sea submersible carries out.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorough study is described by this phrase, and literally a deep-sea vessel works at great depth.

clue.text: Greatly enjoy being skilful and winning

parts.note: to love something is to enjoy it greatly
able means competent or skilled

explanation.surface: A competitor who relishes being good and coming first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winning' looks like victory but means charming.
explanation.definitionFit: A winning manner is charming and endearing, attracting affection.

clue.text: Specifically, what makes blood thicker than water?

definitions.text: Specifically, what makes blood thicker than water?

parts.words: Specifically, what makes blood thicker than water
parts.note: plays on the proverb about family, and on specific gravity, the ratio of a substance's density to water's

explanation.surface: A question about why family ties count more than other bonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Specifically' hints at specific gravity, the physics term; 'relative' also means a family member, the proverb's point.
explanation.definitionFit: Specific gravity is the ratio of a substance's mass per volume to that of water, so blood's is above one.

clue.text: Go over the limits?

parts.note: suggests exceeding bounds, but means walking round a parish boundary

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone has overstepped what is allowed.
explanation.walkthrough: This is an old English parish custom: walking the parish boundary and striking its markers, so 'go over' means walk along, not exceed.
explanation.definitionFit: The custom involves processing along a parish's border, literally going over its limits.

clue.text: Desperate employer tends to repeated and extensive use of manpower

definitions.text: repeated and extensive use of manpower

indicators.note: desperate suggests things in a frantic state, so the following words are shuffled

explanation.surface: A frantic boss leaning on staff again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving staff to new posts again and again is reassigning the workforce, in the plural.

clue.text: Mistake by deserter trapped by signs of hesitation

indicators.note: trapped by says the deserter is held inside the hesitation sounds

parts.note: er and um are the noises people make when hesitating
a rat is someone who abandons a cause, as rats leave a sinking ship

explanation.surface: A deserter caught out because he stammered under questioning.
explanation.walkthrough: One phrase supplies two sounds, which sit on either side of the deserter.
explanation.definitionFit: An erratum is an error in print, listed on a correction slip in a book.

clue.text: A number work out how to delegate

parts.note: D is 500 in Roman numerals
to evolve is to develop or work out gradually

explanation.surface: A manager calculating how to hand tasks down to staff.
explanation.walkthrough: Roman numerals give 'a number' as a single letter, here D.
explanation.definitionFit: To devolve is to pass power or duties down to someone else, which is delegating.

clue.text: Ran lightly towards the top — and stumbled

definitions.meaning: tripping means stepping lightly and nimbly, and up means towards the top
caught a foot and fell or nearly fell

explanation.surface: Someone skipping up the stairs who then lost their footing.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit the phrase: a light-footed run upward, and an idiom for falling over or blundering.

clue.text: Possibly rent a poet's cave

indicators.note: possibly says the letters given could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A poet who might lease a cave to write in.
explanation.definitionFit: Antre is a literary, chiefly poetic word for a cavern, used by Shakespeare in Othello.

clue.text: Going off in great spirits

definitions.meaning: food or game that is starting to rot

explanation.surface: Someone setting off in a cheerful mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat that is spoiling is said to be high, and an elated person is also described the same way.

clue.text: No tipping? Honestly!

definitions.meaning: a surface that does not tilt to either side is flat

explanation.surface: A diner indignant at a no-gratuities policy.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat surface is described with this phrase, and so is a straight-dealing, honest person.

clue.text: Expressing contempt for cocaine taking?

definitions.meaning: making a scornful noise through the nose
inhaling the drug through the nose

explanation.surface: Disapproving of drug use.
explanation.definitionFit: A scornful nasal noise and inhaling powdered drug are both described by the same nasal verb form.

clue.text: Capital ideas

parts.note: capital means excellent, but also suggests the head, where ideas come from

explanation.surface: Splendid suggestions, or thoughts from a nation's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudden clever inspirations are excellent ideas, and they occur in the head, the body's capital.

clue.text: It supplies one's needs at the press of a button

definitions.text: It supplies one's needs at the press of a button

parts.words: It supplies one's needs at the press of a button
parts.note: sounds like a servant or machine, but describes a pressurised spray can

explanation.surface: Praise for some labour-saving gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: A spray can dispenses deodorant, paint or polish when its nozzle is pressed.

clue.text: Delight from being in love with the French language

parts.note: en is French for in
amour is the French word for love

explanation.surface: The joy of being in love with French.
explanation.walkthrough: The French for 'in love', en amour, gives the answer; 'with the French language' tells you both words are French.
explanation.definitionFit: To charm or captivate someone is to delight them; the verb is now usually used in the passive.

clue.text: Extremely nervous

parts.note: on edge, while extremely also hints at being out at the edges

explanation.surface: A description of someone very jittery.
explanation.definitionFit: Being tense and jumpy is being on edge, and the word also playfully suggests being at the extremes.

clue.text: Commanded by junior

explanation.surface: A junior officer serving below a commander.
explanation.definitionFit: Serving beneath someone in command, and being lower in rank, are both expressed by this preposition or adjective.

clue.text: Back stove put in new order

parts.note: the rear is the back part of something
a range is a large kitchen cooker

explanation.surface: Reorganising a kitchen by moving the stove to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: To reorder things is to change their arrangement into a different sequence.

clue.text: One out of bed seen going upstairs

definitions.meaning: someone who gets up, early or late
the vertical part of each step on a staircase

explanation.surface: Someone up and about, seen heading up the stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: An early bird is someone up from sleep, and the upright board of each stair step has the same name.

clue.text: Journals I'd taken back to sign

indicators.note: taken back says the letters of the contraction run backwards

parts.note: the contraction written as its two letters
Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Someone retrieving their journals to sign them.
explanation.definitionFit: Diaries are daily personal records, a common kind of journal.

clue.text: No turning back with change in working

indicators.note: turning back says the word before it is read in reverse

parts.note: the word written as it stands before it is turned
to shift is to alter or move

explanation.surface: A worker refusing to go back and change something.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker currently doing their stint at the factory is on duty, that is, working.

clue.text: Even in peacetime its members are prepared to fight

definitions.text: Even in peacetime its members are prepared to fight

parts.words: Even in peacetime its members are prepared to fight
parts.note: describes a standing professional force kept ready even without a war

explanation.surface: A description of soldiers who stay ready when there is no war.
explanation.definitionFit: A standing professional force of full-time soldiers stays in service between wars, unlike reservists or conscripts.
